verdict.rationale: Fellow's developer docs describe webhooks that send an HTTP POST to a URL you specify when events occur, such as an AI note being generated or an action item being completed. The setup requires your own public HTTPS endpoint, which confirms these are registrable outbound callbacks a program can consume. missing for 10: a full documented event catalog beyond the examples, evidence of payload signing/verification and retry/delivery guarantees, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Webhooks allow you to receive real-time notifications when events occur in Fellow.
When an event happens (like an AI note being generated or an action item being completed), Fellow sends an HTTP POST request to the URL you specify with details about the event.
This enables you to build integrations that react immediately to changes in Fellow, without needing to poll for updates.
